QASHANI:92:2-6/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:2-6/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:2-6/r3.claim: Human striving differs because some incline toward spiritual good under light’s dominance and others sink into evil under darkness.
QASHANI:92:2-6/r3.anchor: لانجذاب بعضكم إلى جانب الروح والتوجه إلى الخير لغلبة النورية

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r1.claim: Sūrah al-Layl pairs with al-Shams; their central themes and inner and outer features correspond so closely that even a general reader can sense the harmony.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r1.anchor: There is no essential difference between the central themes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.claim: Al-Layl develops the preceding sūrah’s claim that the soul succeeds through purification by identifying what corrupts it and how it can be protected and purified.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r2.anchor: the things which contaminate it are explained

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r3.claim: Verses 1–4 use evidence from the outer and inner worlds to establish that Judgment must come: the Hereafter is this world’s counterpart and makes it meaningful.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r3.anchor: The evidence of the world around man and the world within him is presented to show that the Day of Judgement is bound to come.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p346/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p346/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p346/r4.claim: The paired order of creation proves this world has an afterlife counterpart; without it, life is pointless and the righteous and wrongdoers would be treated as equals, contrary to divine wisdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p346/r4.anchor: This is the premise which is substantiated from the oaths sworn in the previous verses

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p346/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p346/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p346/r5.claim: Here saʿy means the consequences of effort, as shown by 53:39–40, rather than effort itself.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p346/r5.anchor: used not only for effort it is also used for the consequences

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p347/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p347/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p347/r1.claim: Shattā is the plural of shatīt, meaning separate or different; human nature and reason require righteous and wrongful deeds to have different outcomes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p347/r1.anchor: requirement of human nature and intellect

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p347/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p347/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p347/r2.claim: Judgment is necessary so good and evil receive different outcomes; without it, people could go free for all deeds, a notion the Qur’an challenges at 23:115 and 68:35–36.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p347/r2.anchor: this world is nothing but a place of merrymaking

QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r4.claim: Human striving differs: people pursue worldly life, desires, status, the afterlife, piety, remembrance, God's approval, or God Himself; others unite bodily obedience, sincerity, nearness, remembrance, good speech, and counsel.
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r4.anchor: وآخر في طلب مولاه . ومنكم : من يجمع بين سعي النفس بالطاعة ، وسعي القلب بالإخلاص

QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r5.claim: Some people strive for their own ruin and the ruin of their worldly life.
QUSHAYRI:v3p426/r5.anchor: ومنهم من سعيه في هلاك نفسه وما فيه هلاك دنياه

SULAMI:v2p398/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p398/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p398/r1.claim: Striving varies: by speech and deed, intention alone, intention with heart and action, for worldly life, for the afterlife, or solely for God; the lowest aims at the transient world and the highest at God, whose striving is never lost.
SULAMI:v2p398/r1.anchor: سمعت منصور بن عبد الله يقول : سمعت أبا القاسم يقول : قال ابن عطاء : هذه الآية تدل على أن من الناس من يكون سعيه بقوله وفعله

SULAMI:v2p398/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p398/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله النهرواني
SULAMI:v2p398/r2.claim: When God dislikes a servant, He makes righteous people and good deeds beloved to him but withholds acceptance and sincerity, and lets wisdom reach his tongue without truthfulness.
SULAMI:v2p398/r2.anchor: سمعت الحسين بن يحيى يقول : قال : أبو عبد الله النهرواني : إذا أبغض الله عبدا أعطاه ثلاثة ومنعه ثلاثا يحبب إليه الصالحين

SULAMI:v2p398/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p398/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p398/r3.claim: The inner meaning is to see one's striving as an allotment from God before creation; its ranks resemble ranks of courtiers and people of intimacy, from seekers and knowers to lovers, those who arrive, and those who take on divine qualities.
SULAMI:v2p398/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : باطن هذه الآية أن يرى سعيه قسمة من الحق له من قبل التكوين

TUSTARI:92:4/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:4/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:92:4/r1.claim: Human endeavors differ: some are sincere and some are mixed with contingencies.
TUSTARI:92:4/r1.anchor: فمنه ما هو خالص ومنه ما هو مشوب بالأحداث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.claim: The surah explains which traits bring the success and failure just mentioned in the previous surah, then warns of the Fire and distinguishes those entering it from those spared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.anchor: ولما ذكر فيما قبلها قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها ، ذكر هنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r7.claim: Saʿy means your pursuits, and shattā means divided and different; the surah then spells out the differing pursuits.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p492/r7.anchor: إن سعيكم: أي مساعيكم، لشتى: لمتفرقة مختلفة، ثم فصل هذا السعي.

FARRA:v3p270/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p270/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p270/r3.claim: The oath's response is that people's striving differs; this was revealed about Abū Bakr and Abū Sufyān.
FARRA:v3p270/r3.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: إن سعيكم لشتى (4) . هذا جواب القسم، وقوله: «لشتى» يقول: لمختلف،

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p531#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p531#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p531#2/r1.claim: People's striving is varied and different.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148/r1.claim: Saʿy means endeavours; the generic verbal noun is plural in sense, which suits shattā as a plural meaning scattered. Alternatively shattā is an abstract noun or adjective, with an implied dhāt, or personification for emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148/r1.anchor: فإن المصدر المضاف يفيد العموم فيكون جمعا معنى ولذا أخبر عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148/r2.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148/r2.claim: Qatada's report makes the verse the answer to the oath; Alusi also allows that the answer is omitted as in earlier examples.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148/r2.anchor: كما أخرجه ابن جرير عن قتادة وجوز أن يكون الجواب مقدرا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p148/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148/r3.claim: The difference among endeavours means that their outcomes and recompense differ.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p148/r3.anchor: والمراد بتفرق المساعي اختلافها في الجزاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r4.claim: The oath’s answer is that people’s efforts differ: one strives to free oneself, another to ruin oneself.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r4.anchor: جواب القسم قوله: {إن سعيكم لشتى} إن أعمالكم لمختلفة، فساع في فكاك نفسه، وساع في عطبها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r5.speaker: أبو مالك الأشعري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r5.claim: The Prophet says everyone starts the day selling themselves, either freeing or destroying themselves.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p442#2/r5.anchor: روى أبو مالك الأشعري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "كل، الناس يغدو فبائع نفسه فمعتقها أو موبقها"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r6.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r6.claim: Ata reports an Ansari’s palm dropped dates into a neighbor’s yard. After its owner refused the Prophet’s Paradise-palm offer, Abu al-Dahdah traded his orchard for it; the Prophet gave the tree to the neighbor, and the revelation contrasts their efforts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r6.anchor: عن عطاء، قال: كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r4.claim: People’s striving is diverse and divided into different paths.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:1-7/r4.anchor: { إن سعيكم لشتى } إن مساعيكم لأشتات مختلفة جمع شتيت

BINTSHATI:v2p97/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p97/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p97/r4.claim: Whatever its occasion, the lesson is universal because the passage directly addresses people generally: their efforts differ.
BINTSHATI:v2p97/r4.anchor: والعبرة على كل حال بعموم اللفظ، والسياق صريح التوجيه إلى عامة الناس

BINTSHATI:v2p103/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p103/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p103/r5.claim: Sa'y literally means walking but implies purposeful work pursued with effort and persistence.
BINTSHATI:v2p103/r5.anchor: فكان السعي بمعنى العمل مع القصد والدأب

BINTSHATI:v2p104/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p104/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p104/r1.claim: Quranic sa'y can denote literal or figurative movement, as with Moses's staff, the magicians' illusion, and believers' light on Judgment Day.
BINTSHATI:v2p104/r1.anchor: نجد الدلالة الأولى للسعي بمعنى المشي والحركة، على الحقيقة أو التخييل والمجاز

BINTSHATI:v2p104/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p104/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p104/r2.claim: Sa'y also means sustained work in pursuit of an aim, as in the passages about accepted deeds, seeking the afterlife, and people whose efforts go astray.
BINTSHATI:v2p104/r2.anchor: كما نجد دلالة السعي على العمل مع الدأب في آيات

BINTSHATI:v2p104/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p104/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p104/r3.claim: Other uses make the directed purpose especially clear, such as striving to ruin mosques or spreading corruption on earth.
BINTSHATI:v2p104/r3.anchor: وواضح أن السعي في آية الليل، هو من العمل الكسبي مع القصد والدأب

BINTSHATI:v2p104/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p104/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p104/r4.claim: Shatta derives from separation and difference; ashtatan denotes scattering, while shatta denotes divergence or variation, which the next verses explain without further interpretation.

BINTSHATI:v2p113/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p113/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p113/r1.claim: The warning of blazing Fire is general, like the statement that human efforts diverge; the next verse specifies that the most wretched person who denies and turns away enters it.
BINTSHATI:v2p113/r1.anchor: والإنذار بنار تلظى، في آية الليل، عام كالعموم المستفاد من الآية قبله

BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.claim: The oath's night, daylight, and creation frame divergent earthly endeavors, then contrasting afterlife fates: the denier's fire and the pious giver's satisfaction.
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا النسق من البيان المعجز، يتم الربط بين المقسم به في أول السورة:

BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r1.claim: After the preceding surah’s account of purified and corrupted souls and Thamud’s fate, people diverge between good and evil while God governs souls through piety and wickedness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r1.anchor: لما بين في الشمس حال من زكى نفسه وحال من دساها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r8.claim: Though people pursue a common end, their beliefs and actions radically diverge; one seeks deliverance and another ruins himself, so their outcomes cannot all be alike.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p445#2/r8.anchor: إن سعيكم } أي عملكم أيها المكلفون في التوصل إلى مقصد واحد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p446/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p446/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p446/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the oath to the preordained divergence of creatures, by which God tests who does best.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p446/r1.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما بين قبل حالهم في الافتراق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p446/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p446/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p446/r2.claim: The divergent efforts connect to the one who purifies or corrupts the soul; the following promise and threat explain that good and evil occur by God’s inspiration and decree.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p446/r2.anchor: قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p446/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p446/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p446/r3.claim: God inspires giving, piety, charity, miserliness, self-sufficiency, and denial; He created people and their deeds, acts without being questioned, and owns guidance and both worlds, against Qadariyya and Muʿtazila.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p446/r3.anchor: فهو سبحانه الملهم للإعطاء والاتقاء والتصدق , والمقدر للبخل والاستغناء والتكذيب

NAHHAS:v5p241/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p241/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
NAHHAS:v5p241/r6.claim: He glosses saʿy as people's deeds.
NAHHAS:v5p241/r6.anchor: قال محمد بن كعب سعيكم عملكم

NAHHAS:v5p241/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p241/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p241/r7.claim: The oath's answer is the statement that people's efforts differ.

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r1.claim: In ʿAbd Allah's reading, the passage has ‘the day when it shines’ and ‘the male and the female,’ omitting ‘what He created.’
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن أبي إسحق

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن عكرمة

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r4.claim: He said the oath ends here and that people's endeavors differ.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#3/r1.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#3/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله : ان سعيكم قال : السعي : العمل

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#3/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#3/r2.claim: Ibn Masud links the revelation to Abu Bakr buying and freeing Bilal, contrasting Abu Bakr's effort with the efforts of Umayya and others; the passage also glosses denying the good as rejecting God's oneness and the hard path as Hell.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود ، انا أبا بكر الصديق اشترى بلالا من امية بن خلف ، ببردة وعشر اواق فاعتقه لله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r1.claim: The summary that human efforts differ builds suspense for the detailed contrast beginning with the giver and God-fearing person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p379/r1.anchor: وفي قوله : { إن سعيكم لشتى } إجمال يفيد التشويق إلى تفصيله بقوله : { فأما من أعطى } ( الليل : 5 ) الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r1.claim: The preceding surah swore by the soul's shaping, meaning the creation of intellect and knowledge; this surah swears by the human body and its sexes. The oath's response is that human efforts differ, with the emphasis on wealth failing in the fall.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r1.anchor: وقد كان القسم في سورة الشمس بتسوية النفس ، أي خلق العقل والمعرفة في الإنسان ، وأما القسم هنا فبخلق جسد الإنسان واختلاف صنفيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r2.claim: سعي literally means brisk, forceful walking and is metaphorically used for work and striving.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r2.anchor: والسعي حقيقته : المشي القوي الحثيث ، وهو مستعار هنا للعمل والكد .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r3.claim: شتى is the plural of شتيت, from severe dispersion, and here means varied conditions and divergent deeds; a line by Taʾabbaṭa Sharran illustrates the expression شتى النوى والمسالك.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r3.anchor: وشتى : جمع شتيت على وزن فعلى مثل قتيل وقتلى ، مشتق من الشت وهو التفرق الشديد يقال : شت جمعهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r4.claim: The address includes all people, believers and unbelievers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r4.anchor: والخطاب في قوله : { إن سعيكم } لجميع الناس من مؤمن وكافر .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p490#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p490#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p490#2/r10.claim: Saʿy means action; people's deeds diverge sharply between what pleases God and what angers Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p490#2/r10.anchor: و «السعي» العمل. فأخبر تعالى مقسما أن أعمال العباد شتى،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p146/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p146/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p146/r1.claim: The oath's answer means people's deeds differ: some work for Paradise and others for Hell.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p146/r1.anchor: إن أعمالكم لمختلفة عمل للجنة وعمل للنار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p146/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p146/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p146/r2.claim: The believer's and unbeliever's efforts differ, and their outcomes diverge afterward.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p146/r2.anchor: سعي المؤمن والكافر مختلف بينهما بعد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p416#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p416#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p416#2/r4.claim: Because the oaths concern opposing things, the sworn subject is also opposed: human beings pursue contrasting deeds, some good and some evil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p416#2/r4.anchor: ولما كان القسم بهذه الأشياء المتضادة كان القسم عليه أيضا متضادا

JISHUMI:v10p7439/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r5.claim: Saʿy means work and earning; shattā means widely scattered or disparate, with related words denoting distance and division.
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r5.anchor: والسعي: العمل والاكتساب. وشتى: متفرق على تباعد ما بين الشيئين

KASHSHAF:92:4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:4/r1.claim: Shattā is the plural of shatīt: people's pursuits are diverse, as the following verses explain.
KASHSHAF:92:4/r1.anchor: جمع شتيت ،   أي : إن مساعيكم أشتات مختلفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766/r6.claim: شتى is the plural of شتيت, meaning different and scattered; the following passage explains how people's endeavors differ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p766/r6.anchor: { شتى } جمع شتيت ، أي : إن مساعيكم أشتات مختلفة

SAMIN-DURR:92:4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:92:4/r1.claim: ‘Inna sa‘y akum la-shatta’ is the oath’s answer, though the answer could instead be omitted as in comparable passages.
SAMIN-DURR:92:4/r1.anchor: هذا جواب القسم. ويجوز أن يكون محذوفا، كما قيل في نظائره المتقدمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r11.claim: Mawardi glosses the varied striving as differing outcomes, with some rewarded in Paradise and others punished in the Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r11.anchor: لمختلف الجزاء , فمنكم مثاب بالجنة , ومنكم معاقب بالنار .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r12.claim: He also reads it as differing deeds: belief and unbelief, virtue and vice, obedience and disobedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r12.anchor: لمختلف الأفعال , منكم مؤمن وكافر , وبر وفاجر , ومطيع وعاص .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r13.claim: A further possibility is differing character, including compassion or cruelty, patience or rashness, generosity or miserliness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r13.anchor: لمختلف الأخلاق , فمنكم راحم وقاس , وحليم وطائش , وجواد وبخيل ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r14.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the verse came down about Abu Bakr and the sons of Umayya and Ubayy ibn Khalaf torturing Bilal; Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal for God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r14.anchor: وروى ابن مسعود أن هذه الآية نزلت في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه , وفي أمية وأبي ابني خلف حين عذبا بلالا

MUQATIL:92:2-6/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:92:2-6/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:92:2-6/r3.claim: Meccans' deeds vary widely between good and evil.
MUQATIL:92:2-6/r3.anchor: يا أهل مكة، يقول: أعمالكم مختلفة في الخير والشر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#5/r1.claim: Human endeavors differ, and the following verses explain how they differ.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#5/r1.anchor: إن عملكم لمختلف وبيان الاختلاف فيما فصل على أثره

QURTUBI-FULL:92:4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:4/r4.claim: The oath's answer is that people's efforts differ; saʿy means action, and one person frees himself while another ruins himself.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:4/r4.anchor: { إن سعيكم لشتى } هذا جواب القسم. والمعنى: إن عملكم لمختلف.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:4/r5.speaker: عكرمة وسائر المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:92:4/r5.claim: They gloss saʿy as work; a Prophetic report describes people as two traders, one buying and freeing himself, the other selling and ruining himself.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:4/r5.anchor: وقال عكرمة وسائر المفسرين: السعي: العمل فساع في فكاك نفسه، وساع في عطبها

QURTUBI-FULL:92:4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:4/r6.claim: Shattā is the plural of shatīt, like marīḍ and maraḍā; it means far apart because the actions differ greatly.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:4/r6.anchor: وشتى: واحده شتيت مثل مريض ومرضى.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:4/r7.claim: The differences may be guidance and error, reward in Paradise or punishment in the Fire, or contrasting traits such as mercy and harshness, generosity and stinginess.

QUTB-ZILAL:92:4/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:4/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:4/r1.claim: People’s efforts differ in nature, motives, direction, and results, so their recompense differs too; good is unlike evil, guidance unlike error, and faith unlike denial.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:4/r1.anchor: والناس في هذه الأرض تختلف طبائعهم

QUTB-ZILAL:92:4/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:4/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:4/r2.claim: People have such different dispositions, tastes, ideas, and concerns that each seems to inhabit a separate world or planet.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:4/r2.anchor: حتى لكأن كل واحد منهم عالم خاص يعيش في كوكب خاص

RAZI:92:4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:92:4/r1.claim: This verse answers the preceding oath: people’s deeds differ, and their recompenses differ accordingly.
RAZI:92:4/r1.anchor: هذا الجواب القسم ، فأقسم تعالى بهذه الأشياء

RAZI:92:4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:92:4/r2.claim: شتى is the broken plural of شتيت and conveys separation: deeds are far apart because some are guidance and others error, leading respectively to Gardens or Fire.
RAZI:92:4/r2.anchor: وشتى جمع شتيت مثل مرضى ومريض

RAZI:92:4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:4/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:92:4/r3.claim: He links the contrast to verses saying Paradise’s people differ from Hell’s people and believers differ from the wicked.
RAZI:92:4/r3.anchor: لا يستوي أصحاب النار وأصحاب الجنة

RAZI:92:4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:4/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:92:4/r4.claim: He also cites the claim that sinners and believers cannot be treated as equal in life or death.
RAZI:92:4/r4.anchor: أم حسب الذين اجترحوا السيئات أن نجعلهم كالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات

RAZI:92:4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:4/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:92:4/r5.claim: A further comparison contrasts shade with scorching heat.

RAZI:92:4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:4/r6.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI:92:4/r6.claim: The exegetes say this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and Abu Sufyan.
RAZI:92:4/r6.anchor: قال المفسرون : نزلت هذه الآية في أبي بكر وأبي سفيان

RAZI-FULL:v31p180/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p180/r1.claim: The oath's answer says human deeds differ greatly in consequence: some lead to guidance and Paradise, others to error and Hell; the verse resembles contrasts in 59:20, 32:18 and 45:21.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180/r1.anchor: أعمال عباده لشتى أي مختلفة في الجزاء

RAZI-FULL:v31p180/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p180/r2.claim: Shatta is the plural of shatit and conveys separation or distance between unlike things.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180/r2.anchor: وشتى جمع شتيت مثل مرضى ومريض

RAZI-FULL:v31p180/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180/r3.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v31p180/r3.claim: Commentators report that the verse was revealed about Abu Bakr and Abu Sufyan.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون : نزلت هذه الآية في أبي بكر وأبي سفيان

STUDYQURAN:92:4/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:4/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:4/r1.claim: Here saʿy means doing or acting: people work either for redemption or perdition, with no in-between.
STUDYQURAN:92:4/r1.anchor: implying that people work for either redemption or perdition and that there is no in-between

ASAD-NOTES:92:1#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:92:1#n2/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:92:1#n2/r1.claim: People pursue good or bad ends, so their actions necessarily lead to divergent consequences, as also suggested at 91:8.
ASAD-NOTES:92:1#n2/r1.anchor: at good and bad ends (cf. note 6 on 91:8) - sc., "and so the consequences of your doings are, of necessity, divergent"

ASAD-NOTES:92:17/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:92:17/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:92:17/r1.claim: Male and female differentiation and the night/day, darkness/light polarity in nature point to divergent human aims, echoing the first ten verses of the preceding surah.
ASAD-NOTES:92:17/r1.anchor: This, together with the symbolism of night and day, darkness and light, is an allusion

TAB-FULL:v24p460/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p460/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p460/r1.claim: Human beings' deeds differ: some disbelieve and disobey, while others believe and obey.
TAB-FULL:v24p460/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إن سعيكم لشتى} [الليل: 4] يقول: لمختلف

TAB-FULL:v24p460/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p460/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p460/r2.claim: Qatadah glosses the people's striving as different or varied.
TAB-FULL:v24p460/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إن سعيكم لشتى} [الليل: 4] يقول: لمختلف

TAB-FULL:v24p460#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p460#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p460#2/r1.claim: This verse is the answer to the oath beginning with the night that veils.
TAB-FULL:v24p460#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: وقع القسم هاهنا {إن سعيكم لشتى} [الليل: 4]

TAB-FULL:v24p460#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p460#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p460#2/r2.claim: Qatadah likewise says that the oath's answer occurs here.
TAB-FULL:v24p460#2/r2.anchor: قال: وقع القسم هاهنا {إن سعيكم لشتى} [الليل: 4]

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:4:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:4:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:4:anmerkung/r1.claim: The use of saʿy is compared with passages in 88:8, 76:22, and 53:39.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:4:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zu s-ʿ-y vgl. 88:8 (li-saʿyihā rāḍiyah), 76:22 (ʾinna hāḏā kāna lakum ǧazāʾan wa-kāna saʿyukum maškūrah), 53:39

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r2.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r2.claim: Neuwirth reads the two elemental pairs as the structural matrix for differing human aims and their corresponding recompense.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r2.anchor: die wiederum gegensätzliche Arten der Vergeltung nach sich ziehen.“ (Neuwirth, „Horizont“, 24)

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r3.claim: As in 91:1–8, the oath presents symmetry and duality as principles structuring both human moral life and all creation; sura 55 later gives this theme special prominence.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:1-4:kommentar/r3.anchor: Wie noch ausführlicher in 91:1–8 stellt die einleitende Schwurpassage damit Symmetrie und Dualität als ein nicht nur die moralische Existenz des Menschen, sondern die gesamte Schöpfung strukturierendes Prinzip dar

TABATABAI:92:2-7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:2-7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:2-7/r5.claim: Saʿy is swift walking and here means purposeful deeds; shatta is a plural meaning dispersed. The oath answers that efforts and their effects diverge, from generosity, piety, and faith to miserliness, self-sufficiency, and denial.
TABATABAI:92:2-7/r5.anchor: السعي هو المشي السريع، والمراد به العمل من حيث يهتم به

TABRISI:92:2-3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:2-3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:92:2-3/r3.claim: Shattā means widely dispersed, as in the expression shattān for two things far apart.
TABRISI:92:2-3/r3.anchor: شتى أي متفرق على تباعد ما بين الشيئين جدا ومنه شتان

TABRISI:92:3-4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:3-4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:92:3-4/r4.claim: The response to the oath is that people's deeds differ: some are destined for Paradise and others for Hell.
TABRISI:92:3-4/r4.anchor: هذا جواب القسم والمعنى إن أعمالكم لمختلفة فعمل للجنة وعمل للنار عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:92:3-4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:3-4/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:92:3-4/r5.claim: Another reading says human efforts are scattered among freeing oneself, self-destruction, worldly aims, and afterlife aims.
TABRISI:92:3-4/r5.anchor: إن سعيكم لمتفرق فساع في فكاك رقبته وساع في هلاكه وساع للدنيا وساع للعقبى

THALABI:v10p216#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p216#3/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p216#3/r5.claim: People's striving differs: one strives to free himself, another to ruin himself, as the Prophet's saying about buying or selling oneself explains.
THALABI:v10p216#3/r5.anchor: إن سعيكم لشتى إن عملكم لمختلف

THALABI:v10p216#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p216#3/r6.speaker: عكرمة وسائر المفسرين
THALABI:v10p216#3/r6.anchor: وقال عكرمة وسائر المفسرين: السعي: العمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77/r1.claim: Human actions differ: some lead to Paradise and others to the Fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إن أعمالكم لمختلفة، عمل للجنة، وعمل للنار (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77/r2.claim: He says the people of Mecca describe people's deeds as differing between good and evil.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77/r2.anchor: يعني أن أهل مكة تقول إن أعمالكم لمختلفة في الخير والشر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77/r3.claim: The meaning of shatta was discussed under the phrase varied plants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77/r3.anchor: وتفسير "شتى" قد سبق في قوله: {من نبات شتى} (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p77/r4.claim: They report that the verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and Abu Sufyan; the passage ends before giving further context.

WAHIDI-QT:92:4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:4/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:4/r1.claim: Human efforts differ: the believer's work and the unbeliever's work are far apart.
WAHIDI-QT:92:4/r1.anchor: إن عملكم لمختلف يريد بينهما بعد يعني عمل المؤمن وعمل الكافر

WAHIDI-QT:92:4/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:4/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:4/r2.claim: The verse was revealed about Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
WAHIDI-QT:92:4/r2.anchor: نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق وأبي سفيان بن حرب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p364/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p364/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p364/r1.claim: A skilled speaker chooses ambiguity or precision to suit the intended meaning; Qur'anic omission of a preposition can deliberately leave several readings open.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p364/r1.anchor: المتكلم البليغ يختار الجملة التي تؤدي المعنى الذي يريده

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p364/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p364/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p364/r4.claim: The contrasting oath elements answer to the varied efforts: people diverge toward Paradise or Fire, across times, actors, states, and outcomes.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p364/r4.anchor: جواب القسم شتى يعني متباين لأن سعينا متباين ومتضاد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p366/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p366/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p366/r1.claim: Unlike al-Qiyama and al-Najm, which detail embryonic development and divine power, al-Layl avoids الزوجين: the word suggests likeness and union, at odds with شتى, which signals separation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p366/r1.anchor: لا يتناسب التماثل مع الافتراق فالزوج هو المثيل والنظير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p366/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p366/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p366/r2.claim: The oath concerns a contested, unseen afterlife outcome, not ordinary worldly work; سعيكم addresses morally responsible people, and the emphatic إن and lām underscore the disputed divergence.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p366/r2.anchor: السعي هنا لا يدل على السعي في أمور الدنيا من التجارة والزراعة والصناعة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p367/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p367/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p367/r1.claim: Al-Layl keeps both its oath and answer unrestricted, unlike al-Shams, which specifies its objects; giving, piety, and الحسنى are likewise left open.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p367/r1.anchor: جواب القسم في سورة الليل (إن سعيكم لشتى) مطلق أيضا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r3.claim: The guidance statement connects to diverse human endeavors: if people sought God's guidance, their striving would not diverge; the next righteous description exemplifies that guidance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r3.anchor: لأنه لو ابتغى الناس الهدى عند الله لما تشتت سعيهم

ELMALILI:92:4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:4/r1.claim: Human endeavors are scattered, inconsistent, and disordered, although well-being and success depend on unity, cooperation, and gathering together.
ELMALILI:92:4/r1.anchor: mesâîniz birbirini tutmaz surette müteferrik, dağınık, nizamsızdır. Hâlbuki hayat ve felah nizâm-ı tevhid ile te‘âvün ve ictimâ‘a merbuttur.

ELMALILI:92:4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:4/r2.claim: Another reading is that people's efforts differ in moral quality and rank: some work well or highly, others badly or poorly, and some believe while others do not.
ELMALILI:92:4/r2.anchor: Yahut sa‘yleriniz çok farklıdır. Kimi iyi çalışır kimi kötü, kimi yüksek kimi aşağı, kimi imanlı kimi imansız.

ELMALILI:92:4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:4/r3.speaker: مفسّرین
ELMALILI:92:4/r3.claim: Exegetes explain shattā as efforts with differing outcomes: faith, obedience, and good deeds versus disbelief, disobedience, and sins.
ELMALILI:92:4/r3.anchor: Müfessirîn burada bunu hükümleri muhtelif, birbirinden uzak, kimi iman ve itaat ve hasenât gibi hayr u hidâyet

ELMALILI:92:4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:4/r4.claim: The verse can also be understood through the contrast of disagreement and agreement, as expressed in the cited statement about those shown mercy.
ELMALILI:92:4/r4.anchor: mazmûnuna göre ihtilâf ve ittifak ile mülâhaza da mümkindir.

ELMALILI:92:4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:4/r5.claim: The clearest purpose is to warn against fragmentation like that of the age of ignorance and to urge unity in thought and ordered action.
ELMALILI:92:4/r5.anchor: asıl murad, câhiliyette olduğu gibi teşettüt ve tefrikanın kendisinden tahzir

ELMALILI:92:4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:4/r6.claim: Fragmented effort is worse than idleness because its mutually cancelling work is futile toil and therefore an evil to avoid.
ELMALILI:92:4/r6.anchor: say‘de teşettüt ve perişanlık yekdiğerini nâkız olmak itibariyle haddizâtında atâletten daha fena olan boşuna bir te‘ab

ELMALILI:92:4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:4/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:4/r7.claim: Conflicting desires and goals disarray hearts through disbelief, idolatry, and sin; failure to affirm God's unity ruins both individuals and society.
ELMALILI:92:4/r7.anchor: Allah’ın birliğine hakkıyla iman edememekten münba‘is olan bu hâl ise ferdin de cemiyetin de perişanlığıdır.

ELMALILI:92:4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:4/r8.claim: The ruin of divided efforts is clarified by the image of an idolater falling from the sky and by disbelievers' deeds scattered like ashes in a storm.
ELMALILI:92:4/r8.anchor: وَمَن يُشْرِكْ بِٱللَّهِ فَكَأَنَّمَا خَرَّ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r17.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r17.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal from Umayya ibn Khalaf for a cloak and ten uqiyyas, after which the opening of this surah was revealed.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r17.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd’dan tahric etmişlerdir, demiş ki

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:1/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:1/r3.claim: People's efforts differ in kind, quality, and purpose, implying human worth depends on religious, moral, and humane conduct rather than sex; this leads into poverty and generosity versus miserliness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:1/r3.anchor: bir insanı değerli veya değersiz yapan unsurun cinsiyet değil, davranışların dinî, ahlâkî ve insanî yönlerden mahiyeti ve değeri olduğu ima edilmiş

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r1.speaker: عبد الله
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r1.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reports that Abū Bakr bought and freed Bilāl; the verse that efforts differ refers to Abū Bakr’s and Umayya b. Khalaf’s contrasting efforts.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله: أن أبا بكر اشترى بلالا من أمية بن خلف ببردة وعشرة أواق من ذهب فأعتقه

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.claim: An alternative contextual account identifies the giver as Abu al-Dahdah and the miser as the Ansari palm owner; it maps ease to Paradise, hardship to Hell, and death to loss of wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى واتقى } يعني أبا الدحداح. { وصدق بالحسنى } أي بالثواب

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r5.claim: Most commentators hold that the sura was revealed about Abu Bakr, as related from Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, and others; another Abu al-Dahdah report is noted at 2:245.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r5.anchor: والأكثر أن السورة نزلت في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه. وروي ذلك عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس وعبد الله بن الزبير وغيرهم

RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r1.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r1.claim: Al-Qaffal says the sura was revealed about Abu Bakr's spending on Muslims and Umayya ibn Khalaf's miserliness and disbelief, while its message applies generally.
RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r1.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله : نزلت هذه السورة في أبي بكر

RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r2.claim: Its general scope is evident from statements that human striving differs and that the audience is warned of a blazing Fire.
RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r2.anchor: إلا أنها وإن كانت كذلك لكن معانيها عامة للناس

TAB:92:4/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:4/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:4/r1.claim: People's deeds differ: some disbelieve and disobey, while others believe and obey.

TAB:92:4/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:4/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:92:4/r2.claim: Qatada glosses the people's striving as different.
TAB:92:4/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  إن سعيكم لشتى يقول :  لمختلف

TAB:92:4/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:4/r3.speaker: author
TAB:92:4/r3.claim: This clause answers the oath: ‘By the night when it covers, your striving is surely diverse’; the learned authorities agree.

TAB:92:4/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:4/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:92:4/r4.claim: Qatada identifies this clause as where the oath's answer falls.
TAB:92:4/r4.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قال :  وقع القسم هاهنا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p349/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p349/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p349/r1.claim: In its basic sense, saʿy is walking quickly, at a pace below running.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p349/r1.anchor: السعي : في الأصل . الإسراع في المشي ، وهو دون العدو

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p349/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p349/r6.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p349/r6.claim: The third sense is deeds or striving: the source applies it both to striving for the afterlife and to people's divergent efforts.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p349/r6.anchor: وذكر المفسرون أنه في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه : -

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r8.claim: The differing saʿy of people means their deeds differ.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r9.claim: The common underlying sense of saʿy is walking and moving quickly.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r9.anchor: وأصل هذا كله: المشي والإسراع فيه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r1.claim: The root shatt denotes separation or difference; in context shattā signals difference opposed to concord, while ashtāt signals dispersion opposed to gathering.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r1.anchor: والشتُّ والشتات في اللغة التفرق والاختلاف

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r2.claim: The Quran uses shattā for diverse plants, divergent human efforts, and hearts that are divided; each context gives the sense of difference.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p233/r2.anchor: ومعنى الاختلاف، المقابل للائتلاف، هم ما يعيطه سياقها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p249/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p249/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p249/r1.claim: The oath does not invoke night and day in general but their perceptible contrast: darkness covering the world against the brightness of day, paralleled by the difference between male and female creation.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p249/r1.anchor: وإذ لم يتعلق البيان القرآني فيهما بغير الغشية والتجلي، نلمح السر البياني فيما تلفت إليه الواو من تقابل واضح محسوس

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p249/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p249/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p249/r2.claim: The visible contrasts of night and day and male and female prepare readers to grasp the moral and unseen contrasts that follow: giving and withholding, guidance and denial, ease and hardship, and the divergent afterlife outcomes.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p249/r2.anchor: توطئة إيضاحية لبيان تفاوت مماثل في معنويات لا تدرك بالحس: {إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّى}

ABUHAYYAN:92:4/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:4/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:4/r1.claim: Saʿy means your endeavors; shattā means scattered or varied, which the next verses explain.
ABUHAYYAN:92:4/r1.anchor: { إن سعيكم } : أي مساعيكم ، { لشتى } : لمتفرقة مختلفة ، ثم فصل هذا السعي

ALUSI:92:4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:4/r1.claim: The annexed verbal noun means all your endeavors, collective in sense, which accounts for the plural predicate shattā.
ALUSI:92:4/r1.anchor: فإن المصدر المضاف يفيد العموم فيكون جمعاً معنى ولذا أخبر عنه بجمع

ALUSI:92:4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:4/r2.claim: Alternatively shattā is a feminine verbal noun, a predicate with an implied dhū, an adjective meaning scattered, or the very notion of separation for emphasis.
ALUSI:92:4/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن لا يعتبر سعيكم في معنى الجمع ويكون شتى مصدراً مؤنثاً

ALUSI:92:4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:4/r3.claim: The different endeavors differ in their recompense.
ALUSI:92:4/r3.anchor: والمراد بتفرق المساعي اختلافها في الجزاء

ALUSI:92:4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:4/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI:92:4/r4.claim: Qatāda, as transmitted by al-Ṭabarī, takes this sentence as the answer to the oath; al-Alūsī also allows an unstated answer.
ALUSI:92:4/r4.anchor: كما أخرجه ابن جرير عن قتادة وجوز أن يكون الجواب مقدراً

BAGHAWI:92:4/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:4/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:92:4/r1.claim: This is the answer to the oath: deeds differ, as some strive to free themselves and others to ruin themselves.
BAGHAWI:92:4/r1.anchor: جواب القسم قوله :{ إن سعيكم لشتىً } إن أعمالكم لمختلفة

BAGHAWI:92:4/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:4/r2.speaker: أبو مالك الأشعري
BAGHAWI:92:4/r2.claim: Abu Malik al-Ashari reports the Prophet saying that everyone starts the day selling himself, either freeing or destroying himself.
BAGHAWI:92:4/r2.anchor: روى أبو مالك الأشعري قال : "  قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : كل الناس يغدو

BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.claim: Ata recounts an Ansari's palm tree whose fallen dates entered a neighbor's home; the Prophet offered a tree in Paradise, the owner refused, and Abu al-Dahdah bought it with his garden and gave it to the neighbor. The report maps the giver to Abu al-Dahdah and the miser to the Ansari.
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.anchor: عن عطاء ،   قال : " كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة وكان له جار يسقط من بلحها في داره

BAYDAWI:92:4/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:4/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:4/r1.claim: People's efforts are different and scattered; shattā is the plural of shatīt.
BAYDAWI:92:4/r1.anchor: إن مساعيكم لأشتات مختلفة جمع شتيت

BIQAI:92:4/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:4/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:4/r1.claim: The address concerns accountable people striving toward a common aim; emphasis marks how surprising it is that effort differs so greatly despite that shared goal.
BIQAI:92:4/r1.anchor: عملكم أيها المكلفون في التوصل إلى مقصد واحد

BIQAI:92:4/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:4/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:4/r2.claim: “Saʿy” is chosen to convey that each person exerts the utmost effort in his work.
BIQAI:92:4/r2.anchor: وعبر بالسعي ليبذل كل في عمله غاية جهده

BIQAI:92:4/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:4/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:4/r3.claim: “Shattā” means sharply different; it is the plural of “shatīt,” like “qatlā” from “qatīl.”

BIQAI:92:4/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:4/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:4/r4.claim: People can mismatch gender and disposition: a man may have a feminine aspiration, and a woman may have masculine action.
BIQAI:92:4/r4.anchor: فيكون الإنسان رجلاً وهو أنثى الهمة

BIQAI:92:4/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:4/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:4/r5.claim: People diverge in belief, speech, and deeds: some seek salvation and others burden themselves with sin; since opposites cannot both please or anger God, the polytheists' excuse that God willed their idolatry fails.
BIQAI:92:4/r5.anchor: فعلم قطعاً أنه لا بد من محق ومبطل

BIQAI:92:4/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:4/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:92:4/r6.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects divergence to God's eternal decree and test, and to the earlier account of the purified and corrupted soul.

BIQAI:92:4/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:4/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:92:4/r7.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says God inspires giving and piety and decrees stinginess and denial; citing God's creation of human deeds and that He is not questioned, he condemns Qadariyya and Muʿtazila.
BIQAI:92:4/r7.anchor: فهو سبحانه الملهم للإعطاء والاتقاء والتصدق

DURR:92:4/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:4/r1.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:92:4/r1.claim: ʿIkrima glosses “saʿy” as deeds or action.
DURR:92:4/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله : { إن سعيكم } قال : السعي العمل

DURR:92:4/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:4/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR:92:4/r2.claim: Qatada says the oath's answer occurs here: people's endeavors are diverse or different.
DURR:92:4/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قال : وقع القسم ههنا { إن سعيكم لشتى } يقول : مختلف

DURR:92:4/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:4/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR:92:4/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal, and that the revelation contrasts Abu Bakr's effort with that of Umayya and Ubayy, identifying faith in the good as monotheism and the hard outcome as Hell.
DURR:92:4/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أن أبا بكر الصديق اشترى بلالاً من أمية بن خلف وأبي بن خلف ببردة وعشر أواق

IBNATIYYA:92:4/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:4/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:4/r1.claim: Saʿy means deeds or work; people's actions are sharply divided, some pleasing God and others provoking His anger.
IBNATIYYA:92:4/r1.anchor: و «السعي » العمل ،   فأخبر تعالى مقسماً أن أعمال العباد شتى ،   أي مفترقة جداً

IBNKATHIR:92:4/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:4/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:92:4/r1.claim: The oaths name opposites, matching the contrast among people's acquired deeds: some do good and others evil.
IBNKATHIR:92:4/r1.anchor: ولما كان القسم بهذه الأشياء المتضادة كان القسم عليه أيضا متضادا ؛ ولهذا قال : { إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّى }

MAWARDI:92:4/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:4/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:92:4/r1.claim: The people's endeavors differ in their outcomes: some are rewarded with Paradise and others punished in the Fire.
MAWARDI:92:4/r1.anchor: أحدهما : لمختلف الجزاء ،   فمنكم مثاب بالجنة ،   ومنكم معاقب بالنار .

MAWARDI:92:4/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:4/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:92:4/r2.claim: Their actions also differ: some are believers and others unbelievers, righteous and wicked, obedient and disobedient.
MAWARDI:92:4/r2.anchor: الثاني : لمختلف الأفعال ،   منكم مؤمن وكافر ،   وبر وفاجر ،   ومطيع وعاص .

MAWARDI:92:4/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:4/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:92:4/r3.claim: Māwardī also suggests that temperaments differ, from compassionate to harsh, mild to reckless, and generous to miserly.
MAWARDI:92:4/r3.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثاً : لمختلف الأخلاق ،   فمنكم راحم وقاس ،   وحليم وطائش ،   وجواد وبخيل .

MAWARDI:92:4/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:4/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:92:4/r4.claim: On the interpretation about differing temperaments, the oath is directed to this point.
MAWARDI:92:4/r4.anchor: وجواد وبخيل .   وعلى هذا وقع القسم .

MAWARDI:92:4/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:4/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI:92:4/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that it was revealed about Abū Bakr and Umayya and Ubayy, the sons of Khalaf, torturing Bilāl for becoming Muslim; Abū Bakr bought Bilāl for a cloak and ten coins and freed him for God.
MAWARDI:92:4/r5.anchor: وروى ابن مسعود أن هذه الآية نزلت في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه ،   وفي أمية وأبّي ابني خلف حين عذّبا بلالاً على إسلامه

NASAFI:92:4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:4/r1.claim: Human effort and deeds differ; the following verses explain the ways in which they differ.
NASAFI:92:4/r1.anchor: إن عملكم لمختلف وبيان الاختلاف فيما فصل على أثره

QURTUBI:92:4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:4/r1.claim: This is the answer to the oath: your deeds are diverse.
QURTUBI:92:4/r1.anchor: " إن سعيكم لشتى " هذا جواب القسم . والمعنى : إن عملكم لمختلف

QURTUBI:92:4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:4/r2.speaker: عكرمة وسائر المفسرين
QURTUBI:92:4/r2.claim: Ikrima and other commentators say سعي means action: one strives to free himself and another to ruin himself.
QURTUBI:92:4/r2.anchor: وقال عكرمة وسائر المفسرين : السعي : العمل ، فساع في فكاك نفسه ، وساع في عطبها

QURTUBI:92:4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:4/r3.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI:92:4/r3.claim: A Prophetic report illustrates the contrast: one person purchases and frees himself, while another sells and destroys himself.
QURTUBI:92:4/r3.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : ( الناس غاديان : فمبتاع نفسه فمعتقها ، وبائع نفسه فموبقها

QURTUBI:92:4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:4/r4.claim: The singular of شتى is شتيت, like مريض and مرضى; differing things are called شتى because they are far apart.
QURTUBI:92:4/r4.anchor: وشتى : واحده شتيت ، مثل مريض ومرضى . وإنما قيل للمختلف شتى لتباعد ما بين بعضه وبعضه

QURTUBI:92:4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:4/r5.claim: People's deeds are far apart: some are error and some guidance, with believers and devout people opposite disbelievers and wicked people, and obedience opposite disobedience.
QURTUBI:92:4/r5.anchor: أي إن عملكم لمتباعد بعضه من بعض ؛ لأن بعضه ضلالة وبعضه هدى . أي فمنكم مؤمن وبر ، وكافر وفاجر ، ومطيع وعاص

QURTUBI:92:4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:4/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:92:4/r6.claim: Another view takes the diversity as differing recompense: some receive Paradise and others punishment in the Fire.
QURTUBI:92:4/r6.anchor: وقيل : " لشتى " أي لمختلف الجزاء ، فمنكم مثاب بالجنة ، ومعاقب بالنار

QURTUBI:92:4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:4/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:92:4/r7.claim: Another view refers to different temperaments, such as merciful or harsh, gentle or rash, generous or miserly.
QURTUBI:92:4/r7.anchor: وقيل : أي لمختلف الأخلاق ، فمنكم راحم وقاس ، وحليم وطائش ، وجواد وبخيل
